title: blf: Use WTAP_ENCAP_NONE, record linktypes must match interface linktype
description:
blf generates its own IDBs, so at the start of a file it should
set the file encapsulation to WTAP_ENCAP_NONE ("hasn't read any
interfaces yet, but will generate its own IDBs") instead of
WTAP_ENCAP_UNKNOWN ("a type unknown to libwiretap, possibly bogus").

This is needed when converting a blf file to pcapng without doing a
two pass read.

See commit ca230a59e05b1a2b89faeaec33e6396c9344c81f

In pcapng, an interface can only have a single linktype, and
the linktype for a record must match the linktype for an
interface.

BLF creates some WIRESHARK_UPPER_PDU records that correspond
to a particular Ethernet interface, but they can't actually share
the same interface (they will have related interface names, with
this one prefixed with "STATUS".)

Fix #19391

notes.body: @LarsVoelker can you check if this works for you?
I am traveling right now. Would it be ok to check this next week and give feedback? Or do you need feedback earlier?
I think next week is fine. It would be good to get it done before 4.2.0. Thanks!

Looks good to me. I am just not so happy that we cannot use the same Interface-ID. I feel like this will make it quite difficult for the user to understand and possibly filter correctly.

Maybe the same name does not make sense. We could prefix the new interfaces:
- ETH-1-2 --> STATUS-ETH-1-2
- ETH-3   --> STATUS-ETH-3

This might make it more obvious that the interface ID is different but allows users to understand what belongs together.

What do you think?

Prefixing with STATUS makes sense.

The only way I can think of to make them have the same interface ID is to make it all WIRESHARK_UPPER_PDU and map the Ethernet packets to the "eth_withoutfcs" dissector or whatever is appropriate.

It all comes back to pcapng being the native format and trying to fit everything else into that structure.
I assume you are preparing the prefixing or should I?
I will update it for the prefixing, no problem.
